Darryn August a selfless hero

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What happen to Darryn August the selfless hero who intervened in a train mugging which left him paralysed from the waist down?

Unique Selling Point:
Darryn August made headlines in April 2017 when he survived being thrown from a MetroRail Train early one morning while travelling to work. Nine men had boarded the carriage and were clearly there to rob people, as they approached two women, one whom was pregnant, Darryn intervened. He was severely beaten and thrown from the moving train. He lay on the side of the track for hours - paralysed and bleeding out. His life was saved by a City of Cape Town cleansing contractor who found him by chance. Darryn's selfless actions and terrible tragedy of being left paralysed from the rib cage down made headlines for weeks. But once the hype was over how did Darryn reconstruct his life?

Summary:
Darryn’s story remains truly inspiring- coming from a poor working class family there was no safety net to help him with expensive re-hab but thanks to his friend Graeme DaleKuys who on hearing of his incredible bravery decided he had to step up. Through Back-a- buddy Graeme set out to raise R50 000 for Darryn and ended up raising half a million. Graeme and a few friends rode what they called the Everest Challenge – the 8884 meters from sea level to the Steenbras Dam viewpoint a ride that started at 4am and ended at 10pm with 46 trips up and down– the equivalent of Everest. Graeme campaign gave people a way to support Darryn for his bravery.
Once he was out of rehab Darryn wanted to find and confront his attackers. The police investigation was not making progress so he started to visit the area where the gang had got onto the train, a small community called Macassar. After weeks of searching he finally sat down with the men that had robbed and thrown him from the train. They were grown men aged between 29 and 36. At first they were defensive and showed no remorse- robbing people was what they did, but after several hours these grown men were crying. All Darryn wanted from them was to confront what they had done to his life; he didn’t press charges because he knows prison doesn’t change people in fact it makes them better criminals. Darryn had grown up in a community filled with men like this and had no illusions about life. His mother -a rape survivor persuaded him not to press charges and inflict suffering in another life but to rather move on with his life.

Darryn continues to work with street kids and youth at risk using his own life story to inspire them. But life as a disabled person is extremely tough especially in areas with pavements and roads that are poorly maintained. Darryn is campaigning to raise awareness for people with disability in poor communities and is assisting the Brandon Beack Foundation support people is disadvantaged communities.

Press Release:


Thrown from a Moving Train
In April 2016 Darryn August was left paralysed after being violently flung from a moving train in an attempt to protect a pregnant woman from gangsters. This real-life superhero’s story of bravery has since inspired people across the nation and he’s received waves of support from fellow South Africans. But is there more to this story?


Script:


Script: It’s well known that riding on the trains in Cape Town can be seriously dangerous. If it’s not people falling from trains because of overcrowding then they are being robbed by gangs when the carriages are quite.
John Link “It was an ordinary start to the day for Darren who like many Capetonians caught the train into work and while train travel is never 100% safe in the City he could never have imagined just how tragically that journey would end
Darryn “One thing led to another, they confronted me I confronted them … they jumped me and gave me quite a hard blow to my head and to my back one of the guys decided to throw me out with the help of the other guys as well as just as I left the train doors I blacked out
Script: Darryn was lying there for two hours before Andrew Dreyer and his team of men who were clearing the siding found him. Initially they though he was a vagrant sleeping it off beside the track.
Andrew “Even before I could ask him he said to me they threw him out of the train what actually transpired according to him they wanted to rob a lady a pregnant lady and so he intervened If my memory serves me correctly they stabbed the back although I didn’t see any blood
Script: In terrible agony Darryn’s was paralysed from the waist down. His story was quickly picked up by the media and family and friends harnessed the public outrage and began a crowd funding campaign . Graeme Kuys a friend from Bible college, and his cousin, raised half a million rand in a matter of weeks. They called it Everest for August.
Link “Darryn’s story struck a chord with many South Africans because he became the everyday super hero standing up against injustice. Back a buddy was the ideal platform for them to show their support
Script: Back a Buddy CEO Patrick Schofield says they have raised 50 million rand for over 3000 causes and Darryn’s has been one of the most successful
Patrick “He is the kind of person who all of us would like to be that when you see someone in need you will stand-up and say no … he experienced extreme trauma himself and in that space there we recognise him as a hero we saw the price he had paid and SA in general said we will stand by you now
Darryn “ I know what it is like to be robbed I know what it is like to be hurt by other people so I don’t think I am a hero I think I am just a normal guy who wants to do the right thing
Script: It’s now 20 months since the accident and Darren continues to give inspiring interviews about working with youth at risk, and forgiving those who had crippled him. We wanted to highlight some of his campaigns
John: Do you recall the impact the pain?
Darryn “I think it is one of the most shocking experiences I have ever had in my life to not be able to move my feet or to get up like I wanted to get up.
Script: Darryn was frustrated by the slow progress police were making on his case so hired a private investigator who he says tracked down his attackers and he had 3 hour meeting with them at the Macassar police station.
John; You tracked down the people who did this to -How did they respond to you
Darryn “Well so sitting down with them and speaking with them was at first a bit intimidating there was a lot of emotion a lot of arrogance to them at first but I never thought I would see this guy with this bad tattoos cry or show that kind of emotion
John “You decided not to press charges and I understand was because in some way it was down to your mother
Darryn “She said that it’s not in your hands whether to make somebody else’s life extremely difficult
Script: Sadly his mother had passed away and once again donations came flooding in from Cape Talk listeners and Golden Arrow with buses for the mourners.
John “I understand you have ambitions to appear in the Paralympics?
Darryn’ 13 07 31 18 either the 2020 Paralympics or beyond and once I get the qualifications all right
Script: While filming at the site of the accident a train approached and slowed down to a crawl, suddenly it dawned on us what might have happened. We were already had misgivings about all the stories that didn’t tie up
Darryn The doctors said if I had to be there a little bit longer I would probably have bled out and I would definitely would have died.
Script: Andrew was the first person at the scene
Andrew “I didn’t see any blood so I am not sure what blood he is referring to
John “and when the paramedics arrived you didn’t see any blood
“ I also didn’t see any blood:
Script: Medical records show there were no stab wounds
Derek “we set out to tell an inspiring story of a young man’s incredible bravery which has had massive and ongoing media coverage and generous public support then we spent weeks checking on the details hoping that we were wrong but the more people we spoke to the more things didn’t quite tie up
Script: When we called the parasport trainers at Stellenbosch University to film Darren riding we were surprised to learn no one had ever heard of him

Script. Then we tracked down the police officer who visited Darryn in hospital but he told her he didn’t want to press charges for religious reasons and so it wouldn’t stand up in court. Darryn told us the police did nothing to track his attackers that’s why he hired private investigator
Link: This is where Darryn says he had a 3 hour meeting with the men who beat him up and threw him from the train. But the Colonel who has been stationed here for the two years says that meeting never took place there is only one meeting room and it’s locked all day after the morning conference. And by now we were not surprised to hear that the gangsters Bloed, Dood and Smiley didn’t ring any bells for the Colonel
Script: We were keen to film his widely reported youth work and followed up the list of names and organizations but not one checked out
Derek “ Darryn says he works with various organizations in Athlone looking after youth at risk and one of his claimed projects is an organic garden here at Blossom Primary we checked it out an Darryn has apparently has never worked in this garden before or after his accident
Script: Darryn had agreed in person to a follow up interview
Derek “We have got an appointment with Darryn for 10
Lauren “But he is not here he left for work
Derek “But Robin you heard us making the arrangement for 10 oclock this morning
Robin “Yes on Monday Darryn said yes he is going to be here but I don’t know
Script: While we waited for Darryn to return we tried finding anyone who could corroborate his story
Derek : Most importantly we have been trying to find Maria the pregnant women that he defended again not much luck there but we will keep trying
Derek: Darryn how you doing its Derek from Carte Blanche we came to chat to you at 10oclock we have come back at 12.30 won’t you give me a call on this number
Derek Link: This is the spot where Darryn was found, its where the trains slows down coming into Somerset West station. Darryn was a fit young surfer before the accident- so the question is did he actually jump from the train to avoid paying for the ticket and things went terribly wrong?
Script: Bernard Moses commutes from Somerset West station every day
Derek “Bernard what have you observed as you see the train coming into Somerset West Station?
Bernard “So it’s quite often that you see people trying evade the fairs by jumping off the train before it actually gets into the station it’s definitely a reality
Derek”16 but some do jump the train just to avoid paying for the ticket
Bernard R7.50 is what their life is worth to them R7.50
Derek Link: This is the station where the pregnant women and other passengers got off he says a number of people were robbed on the train but nobody reported an incident and even after Darryn’s name hit the headlines not a single person came forward to tell the story. In fact there are no eyewitness accounts
Bernard” I mean there is various metrorail groups on facebook as well and I am part of a couple of them and no mention was made of it what’s so ever.
Script: Metrorail have no witness statements and Darryn refused to speak to them on the advice of his lawyer. Despite telling us he wasn’t suing Metrorail his lawyer says he’s having medical assessments to quantity the claim.
Derek “we are sorry to come back we started with an inspiring story but nothing checks out. Did you do any research?
Patrick “our vetting process that we have to protect against this kind of this is very stringent what we do do if someone phones in with a medical condition we ask for doctors records he did break his back it was an extraordinary story which was picked up by multiple different news agents and we were one of them that didn’t see through
Derek: “But we are crushing a story of heroism
Patrick” if you had put that campaign up and said I fell off a train and I broke my back it would have been a powerful story in which people would have contributed the sadness has come through where he probably embellished it into something more than he was
Derek “Its one thing when a young man in a wheel chair tells you a tragic story to your face and it doesn’t quite pan out the problem is the story has gone viral Darryn is being celebrated virtually internationally and money is being raised on the back of that story
Derek” Patrick what do you need to do now
Patrick”We will most definitely contact him regarding this what we will also do is let all the donors know and we will speak to the faith based organization and ask how much of the funds are there
Derek It’s the day we are giving it one more try it’s a quarter past 11 in the morning We really did want to hear Darryn’s side of the story but this is the 4th time and we had an appointment originally

metadata.Summary: Darryn’s story remains truly inspiring- coming from a poor working class family there was no safety net to help him with expensive re-hab but thanks to his friend Graeme DaleKuys who on hearing of his incredible bravery decided he had to step up. Through Back-a- buddy Graeme set out to raise R50 000 for Darryn and ended up raising half a million. Graeme and a few friends rode what they called the Everest Challenge – the 8884 meters from sea level to the Steenbras Dam viewpoint a ride that started at 4am and ended at 10pm with 46 trips up and down– the equivalent of Everest. Graeme campaign gave people a way to support Darryn for his bravery. Once he was out of rehab Darryn wanted to find and confront his attackers. The police investigation was not making progress so he started to visit the area where the gang had got onto the train, a small community called Macassar. After weeks of searching he finally sat down with the men that had robbed and thrown him from the train. They were grown men aged between 29 and 36. At first they were defensive and showed no remorse- robbing people was what they did, but after several hours these grown men were crying. All Darryn wanted from them was to confront what they had done to his life; he didn’t press charges because he knows prison doesn’t change people in fact it makes them better criminals. Darryn had grown up in a community filled with men like this and had no illusions about life. His mother -a rape survivor persuaded him not to press charges and inflict suffering in another life but to rather move on with his life. Darryn continues to work with street kids and youth at risk using his own life story to inspire them. But life as a disabled person is extremely tough especially in areas with pavements and roads that are poorly maintained. Darryn is campaigning to raise awareness for people with disability in poor communities and is assisting the Brandon Beack Foundation support people is disadvantaged communities.
